judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (coordinate rank 0) but in different terms and skill areas: the second SFI is Grade R Term 1, Emergent Writing / Emergent Handwriting ('Develops directionality: moves parts of the body to the left or right, up or down etc.'), while the first SFI is Grade R Term 2, Emergent Reading / Emergent reading skills ('Develops correct eye movement such as following a ball moved from left to right'). The shared content is substantive, not merely lexical: establishing left/right (and up/down) directionality through gross body movement is the broader perceptual-motor base that supports the narrower, later ocular-tracking skill of following a moving object left-to-right, which in turn underpins print tracking. The direction second_to_first runs Term 1 to Term 2 within the same grade, which is the permitted within-grade developmental order; the reverse would be an invalid later-to-earlier term direction. Confidence is moderate because the link is inferred from the shared directionality construct and LC tags ('directionality', 'left and right' vs 'eye movement', 'left to right', 'tracking') rather than an explicit curriculum dependency statement, and source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each).

judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade R (rank 0), Term 4, Skill Area Emergent Writing, Sub-strand Emergent Handwriting, printed as separate bullets in the same table row 4 on page 56; shared ancestry and page proximity alone are not decisive, so the statement texts govern. 'Forms letters with a variety of writing tools such as crayons, pencils, chalk' targets letter formation across varied media and tool handling, while 'Forms some lower case letters correctly, that is, starts and ends in the correct place' targets directional accuracy on a limited ('some') set of lower case letters. These are complementary facets of the same emergent handwriting capability taught concurrently in one term, not an extension in scope, independence, text length or complexity of one over the other, so no developmental dependency is justified in either direction (and same-Grade, same-Term buildsTowards would require substantive extension evidence that is absent). The pair-specific coherence is nevertheless real and instructionally useful — tool control and correct formation reinforce each other within Emergent Handwriting, confirmed by shared LC tags 'emergent writing', 'handwriting', 'letter formation' rather than mere word overlap — so symmetric relatesTo is the correct judgment with canonical endpoint order preserved and null direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context warnings, which are retained and limit but do not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under the same Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 3, WRITING / Handwriting sub-strand and the same source table row (page 76), so hierarchy and page proximity alone are not decisive. The substantive difference is unit of production: 'Copies and writes words with correct spacing' (LCs: copies/writes words with correct spacing; tags copying, handwriting, spacing, words) operates at word level and establishes letter formation plus inter-word spacing, while 'Copies and writes short sentences correctly' (LCs: copies/writes short sentences correctly; tags copying, handwriting, sentences) extends the same copying/writing control to connected multi-word strings where correct spacing is a precondition. Controlled, correctly spaced word writing therefore supports success in copying and writing whole short sentences correctly, justifying a same-Grade, same-Term developmental direction from the word-level skill to the sentence-level skill. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, so this is an inference from the available bullet text and LCs rather than the full source row.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading under the printed Sub-strand 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness', with the first anchored to Term 2 ('Identifies rhyming words in well known rhymes and songs') and the second to Term 4 ('Divides multisyllabic words into syllables: crocodile - croc-o-dile') per their identity_scope_values. The direction is therefore the permitted earlier-to-later Term order within one grade. This is not mere repeated wording: rhyme identification is a holistic, recognition-level sound-pattern skill in familiar oral rhymes and songs, while syllable division requires the child to actively segment an unfamiliar spoken word into its parts (LC tags 'segmenting', 'syllables', 'multisyllabic words' versus 'rhymes', 'rhyming', 'songs'). Attending to and matching word-level sound patterns plausibly supports success in the more analytic oral segmentation task later in the year, so proficiency in the first supports the second. Evidence limits noted: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, but the non-fallback statement text, resolved Grade coordinates and term scoping are sufficient and non-contradictory.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 1 (rank 1), Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', Sub-strand 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes' (Phonics), so the finer within-grade Term order governs direction. The second SFI is Grade 1 Term 3 ('Uses consonant blends to build up and break down words', with LCs for building up and breaking down words with r/l blends, in the table row that revises single letters and introduces common consonant blends and digraphs); the first SFI is Grade 1 Term 4 ('Builds words using sounds learnt', in the row that introduces new consonant blends and continues word building). The Term 3 work establishes blending/segmenting with a specific, taught blend set; the Term 4 statement broadens this to constructing words from the full accumulated repertoire of sounds learnt, so Term 3 proficiency supports success in Term 4. Direction is therefore earlier Term to later Term (second_to_first); the reverse Term 4 to Term 3 direction would be invalid within one grade. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so this is an inferred curriculum progression rather than verified prerequisite truth, but the non-truncated statement text, identity scopes and LC tags ('phonics', 'word building'/'building words') are consistent and sufficient.

Same-rank, same-Term buildsTowards requires substantive extension evidence that is absent here, and the nomination's rank_gap 0, page_gap 0 proximity signals are not semantic direction evidence. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Listening and Speaking (Oral) Skill statements under the same 'Daily activities in all areas of Language and other subjects' sub-strand. The second SFI is Term 1 ('Sings simple songs and does actions (with help)', LCs tagged singing/songs/actions, with explicit scaffolded examples), while the first SFI is Term 3 ('Sings songs and rhymes and performs actions on own', LCs 'Sings songs and rhymes' and 'Performs actions on own' tagged independence). Within Grade R this is an earlier Term to a later Term, and the change is substantive rather than mere repeated wording: from simple songs with adult help to songs plus rhymes performed independently. Proficiency in the Term 1 scaffolded singing-with-actions supports success in the Term 3 independent, broadened version, so buildsTowards runs from the second (Term 1) to the first (Term 3) endpoint. Both endpoints' source evidence lists are truncated (24 omitted items each), but the printed statement texts, terms and Learning Components supplied are sufficient and consistent.

Judgment rests on bounded excerpts: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Skill bullets in Listening and Speaking (Oral) under the same printed sub-strand 'Uses language to think and reason' (first: Term 1, 'Identifies and describes similarities and differences'; second: Term 3, 'Identifies parts from the whole (e.g. parts that make up a picture)'). They are coherent, complementary oral-reasoning operations sharing an 'identifies' LC tag and a 'reasoning' tag, and both rest on perceptual/attribute discrimination. However, part-whole analysis is a distinct reasoning operation rather than a deepening, extension or broadening of comparing similarities and differences: the evidence shows no increase in text length, independence, or scope that would make proficiency in the Term 1 bullet specifically support success in the Term 3 bullet. Term 1-to-Term 3 ordering within Grade R alone is not progression evidence, and the LC/text overlap is thin (jaccard ~0.06, single shared token 'identifies'). Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment; note that source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the first SFI's LC evidence is truncated, so some corroborating detail is outside this bounded excerpt.

Same-rank direction is supported by pair-specific content rather than wording alone: the first SFI establishes the foundational understanding that pictures and photographs carry meaning about events, people, places and things and the oral capacity to talk about that meaning (LCs: 'Understands that pictures and photographs convey meaning...', 'Talks about the meaning conveyed by pictures and photographs'). judgment.rationale: Both Skills are the identical CAPS bullet 'Reads aloud to a partner' sitting under the same Sub-strand (Paired/Independent Reading), Skill Area (READING AND PHONICS) and Term (Term 2), with the first endpoint scoped to Grade 3 (rank 3) and the second to Grade 2 (rank 2). This is substantive conceptual coherence: the same paired oral-reading routine is deliberately carried forward into the adjacent grade within the identical sub-strand, which is meaningful instructional reinforcement rather than incidental repetition of similar words. However, the bounded evidence supplies no pair-specific indication of expanded capability: the statement text, normalized descriptions, the single shared Learning Component (391a7411) and its tags ('paired reading', 'partner', 'reading aloud') are identical, and the nomination evidence is entirely lexical/LC overlap (token, trigram and LC jaccard 1.0) plus a weak local_rank_proximity signal. Any increase in text difficulty or independence at Grade 3 would have to be inferred from the grade label alone, which does not meet the requirement of a substantive, evidenced extension for buildsTowards in this deliberately repetitive curriculum. The judgment is therefore symmetric relatesTo with null direction, preserving canonical endpoint order. Limitation: both endpoints' source evidence and supporting LC evidence are truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so a grade-specific difficulty contrast present in the full source cannot be excluded.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0) under EMERGENT WRITING / 'Emergent Handwriting:' and share the same stated outcome of developing fine-motor control; the first is Term 1 ('uses scissors to cut fringes on paper mats etc.'), the second is Term 3 ('playing more finger rhymes with finger actions'). The term order would permit a Term 1 -> Term 3 buildsTowards, but the two bullets name distinct, parallel activity modalities (scissor cutting versus finger rhymes with actions); the 'more' in the Term 3 statement extends prior finger-rhyme work, not scissor work, so scissor proficiency is not evidenced as supporting the later skill. This is meaningful reinforcement of a shared fine-motor/emergent-handwriting strand rather than a justified developmental dependency, so relatesTo is the supported judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), limiting any stronger developmental claim.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are the identical CAPS bullet 'Continues to build a sight vocabulary from the incidental reading programme, the graded reading series and high-frequency word lists' under the same Skill Area (Reading and Phonics) and Sub-strand (Group Guided Reading), and they share the single Learning Component 573d4f00. The source refs place the first in Grade 1 / Term 2 (rank 1) and the second in Grade 2 / Term 4 (rank 2), so direction is lower-to-higher grade, matching the only permitted buildsTowards direction. This is explicitly cumulative ('continues to build') sight-vocabulary acquisition: the Grade 2 Term 4 instance draws on a more advanced graded reading series and longer high-frequency word lists (its surrounding row covers self-correcting strategies and independent monitoring), so Grade 1 sight-word proficiency supports success at the Grade 2 Term 4 expectation. Judgment rests on expanded grade-level capability, not on the repeated wording alone. Source and LC evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.
